sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict region_only: insert_after_residue 301 -> NULL; the paper names a region, not a junction (region: between the extracellular and transmembrane domains (mouse Cd1d1; ~S301|M302 in human)). Paper (PMID 35874748): "inserting the SortA peptide recognition motif LPETG together with a glycine-/serine-based linker between the extracellular and the transmembrane domain of mouse Cd1d1". Audit note: Secondary sources checked: PMC9301999 full text and its Europe PMC supplementary files (DataSheet_1.docx, Table_1.xlsx, Table_2.xlsx, figure files) contain no primers, construct sequence or residue numbers; data availability statement lists only ProteomeXchange PXD034366/PXD034495, no plasmid deposit. Junction remains an inference from the mouse EC/TM boundary (mouse 305|306 ~ human S301|M302).] L2 explicitly places the insertion 'between the extracellular and the transmembrane domain' of mouse Cd1d1; for human CD1D the EC domain ends at residue 301 (S) and the TM begins at 302 (M), making 301|302 the unique EC/TM junction. The GS linker included in the construct provides physical spacing from the TM helix, and successful cell-surface sortagging confirms extracellular accessibility. Because the source is a mouse ortholog and no residue number is given, the position is classified as inferred rather than validated. Mouse Cd1d1 (close ortholog of human CD1D) was engineered with an LPETG SortA recognition motif plus a glycine/serine-based linker inserted between the extracellular domain and the transmembrane domain of the full-length, membrane-anchored protein, expressed in cells and subjected to cell-surface sortagging.
sites.residue_label: between the extracellular and transmembrane domains (mouse Cd1d1; ~S301|M302 in human)
